data.turoyo: Bdalle gdayši ʕal al lašat w kmahzəmi kmičoki ba mʕare, kmičoki baʕ ʕəṣyanat, kəzzən laʕ ʕitawoṯo, lə manfaʕlalən mede.
data.translation: Sie stolperten nun über Leichen, sie flohen und zogen sich zurück in Höhlen, sie zogen sich zurück in Stellungen, die man verteidigen konnte, in die Kirchen, doch das nutzte ihnen nichts.

rationale: First Preterit box: negative utility with an overt plural beneficiary. Retain -la-lən without inventing agreement.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (58/107)

data.turoyo: Hiye lə manfaʕla gabe. Kḥoyər b aḏnoṯe di səstayḏe w kəmhaləx raṣṭ. Hul d aṯi, maxlaṣle ak kefe komanək.
data.translation: Aber das nützte bei ihm nichts. Er blickte auf die Ohren seiner Stute und ritt gerade zu, bis er aus den schwarzen Steinen herausgekommen war.

rationale: First Preterit box: feminine hiye/manfaʕla and gabe contrast with ordinary Infectum utility; the surrounding reaction is retained to make the context readable.
The quantified amount ḥamšo quruš is the value complement of kmanfəʕ, without a beneficiary or useful purpose. One clear attestation; append after sense 1.

data.translation: Jetzt ist er keine fünf Groschen mehr Wert.

rationale: Only attestation of the new monetary-value construction; compact complete clause with the amount overt.

summary: Move 71/66 from the translation to refs
rationale: The citation and trailing semicolon are inside translation while refs is empty. 71/66 confirms hawxa lo komanfəʕ. Preserve the entry’s translation.

summary: Restore s in the word for fist blows
rationale: 67/51 has bak kulməskat. The entry substitutes z for s, which is not one of the specified normalization conventions.

summary: Utility predicates have the useful entity or situation as subject and the beneficiary in an l-series suffix, an independent eli phrase, or a locative/social frame such as gabe. Purpose l- (speech, a use, a role) is distinct from the personal beneficiary; 81/8 contains both.
The inherited Infectum cell already has five examples. Most proposed better contexts repeat those frames; no further routine utility examples are added.

Two actual manfaʕla-based forms establish the missing Preterit box. Beneficiary marking is not evidence of a new transitive causative sense; the Arabic II etymological label is not a Turoyo stem assignment.
56/110 alone securely places a monetary amount directly after kmanfəʕ. At 58/183 the value judgement uses ṭowən in a separate clause; that passage is not a second attestation of nfʕ sense 2.

The terminal -ne in some plural utility forms and -yo in others are recorded without assigning an additional affected object. Feminine discourse referents need not yield a transparently segmented feminine form before every suffix sequence.
Confirm the -la-lən segmentation of manfaʕlalən at JTM 3.2/5 and the antecedent/agreement of hiye/manfaʕla at 58/107.
Does mede supply the grammatical subject of kmanfəʕ at JTM 4.2/15, with fire as discourse topic?
Clarify the final -ne in 58/183, -yo and subject reference at 98/80, and default versus feminine agreement at 102/17 and 102/32.
Confirm the agreement and beneficiary contraction of gədmanfaʕʕe with i štaġaliye at 115/77.
Confirm the productivity of the monetary-value construction from another speaker or text; the published machine-proposed sense currently has one attestation.

rationale: After hat, the perfect construction requires weggegeben. The edition has er hat sie weggegeben.

summary: Utility includes a remedy working, a person or animal being suitable, an abstract status being of use, and an action failing to achieve its intended effect. Harm from fire is an intended effect in a negative clause, not a new meaning “harm”.
